description_full: Borr Drilling Limited operates as an offshore shallow-water drilling contractor to the oil and gas industry in the Americas, Southeast Asia, West Africa, the Middle East, North Africa, and Europe. It owns, contracts, and operates jack-up rigs for operations in shallow-water areas, such as the provision of related equipment and work crews to conduct oil and gas drilling and workover operations for exploration and production. It serves oil and gas exploration and production companies, such as integrated oil companies, state-owned national oil companies, and independent oil and gas companies. The company was formerly known as Magni Drilling Limited and changed its name to Borr Drilling Limited in December 2016. Borr Drilling Limited was incorporated in 2016 and is based in Hamilton, Bermuda.

financial_summary: Borr Drilling Limited is a small-cap energy business with a $1.3B market cap on $1.0B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +32% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.8× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 14.0% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 18% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
